source: ScienceDirect (May 2025): 'Time-varying performance of betting against beta (BAB) and other risk-based anomalies: Evidence from Asia'
title: H205 Risk Flag: BAB Performance Is Regime-Conditional — Works in Downturns, Reverses in Upturns
summary: A May 2025 study (ScienceDirect) examining BAB and related risk-based strategies across 5 Asian markets (1999-2021) finds that 'betting against risk' strategies (BAB, IVOL, MAX, tail risk) work only during market downturns, while 'betting for risk' (holding high-beta) works better during upturns. This regime-dependence — not a problem in long-run BAB studies — is directly relevant to H205. If BAB alpha concentrates in downturns and TOM windows both cluster at month-end, there may be an interaction: TOM windows during bear market regimes could generate abnormally high BAB returns, while TOM windows in bull regimes might reduce the H205 edge. Mechanism: investor disposition effect (risk-seeking in downturns, risk-averse in upturns). US evidence is not confirmed in this study (Asia only), but the regime-conditional pattern suggests H205 should be analyzed with a market-regime subsample split (bull vs bear, defined by SPY being above/below 200-day MA) to assess robustness. This is a secondary risk flag, not a disqualifier — the H201 TOM confirmation is in US large-cap (SPY), not in Asian markets.
